The problem

Titanic:
The Unsinkable Experience

Ask in plain English

A local LLM answers with pandas. Every number must be exact.

Predict survival

Compare 4 models honestly. Explain where you stand.

Goal: turn a classic 891-row table into something a team would actually want to explore, while showing two serious techniques under the theatre: an LLM agent that calls a tool, and a classic ML comparison. Constraint: everything runs locally (Ollama), and the chatbot’s numbers must be right.

Titanic · Tech talk2
Columns: PassengerId, Survived, Pclass, Name, Sex, Age, SibSp, Parch, Ticket, Fare, Cabin, Embarked. Age is missing for 177 passengers; we impute it by title median for plotting and by median in the model pipeline. Title extraction (Mr, Mrs, Miss, Master, Rare) carries a lot of signal: it encodes sex, age group and status at once.

Titanic · Tech talk3
Two engines behind one FastAPI app. Left lane: the Telegraphist. chat.py runs the tool-calling loop against Ollama; the model’s only tool is query_data, implemented in safe_query.py, which evaluates one read-only pandas expression on the DataFrame. Right lane: the Bridge. model.py trains and compares four classifiers and saves the winner to model.joblib, which is retrained automatically if missing. The frontend is plain HTML/CSS/JS, no build step.

One tool for Python, deps and scripts

$ uv run capture.py     # screenshots
1

2

3

Console script titanic-app

4

capture.py: PEP 723 inline deps, so Playwright never enters the app

Titanic · Tech talk4
Runtime dependencies: fastapi, uvicorn[standard], jinja2, httpx, pandas, scikit-learn, joblib. Dev group: pytest and httpx2. The build backend is uv_build with module-root set to empty, so the package lives in app/ at the root. capture.py declares Playwright in a PEP 723 script header, so uv run capture.py builds an isolated environment for it and the app’s pyproject stays untouched. Gotcha on Windows: a running titanic-app.exe locks the script, so uv add fails until the server stops.

The regatta

Gradient Boosting wins on 5-fold CV.

RF 84.2 · SVM 83.5 · LogReg 82.8
Baseline 61.6

Each ship sails to its mean cross-validated accuracy after a grid search. The axis is zoomed (80 to 86 percent), and labelled. The top three are within 1.3 points, so the honest takeaway is that feature engineering does most of the work. Best Gradient Boosting: 250 trees, learning rate 0.1, depth 2. Every fold and hyperparameter is in the logbook table under the race.

The app running · 4 of 4

You among the 891

POST /predict

You are the gold star, linked to your 5 nearest passengers.

Nearest in the model’s feature space. Colour plus shape: ● survived, ✕ perished.

The default ticket: a 28-year-old third-class man paying £8.05 gets 10 percent. His five nearest neighbours paid the same fare and all perished. A 36-year-old first-class woman gets about 97 percent. The survived/perished palette was checked for colour-blind separation and contrast on the dark background, and the second marker shape means colour is never the only signal.

LLM + one tool

The tool-calling chatbot

1

Question

Plain English, plus recent history

2

qwen3.5:4b

Thinks, then calls the tool

3

Sandbox

One expression, AST-checked, on a copy of df

4

Reply

Dramatic telegram, ends in STOP

5

Number guard

Every figure must match a tool result

>>> (df.Sex == "female").sum()
→ 314
✓ verified↻ corrected= exact figures

7 of 8 test questions passed on the first try.

Titanic · Tech talk9
The sandbox parses with ast in eval mode, so imports and statements cannot exist. It blocks dunder names and attributes, file and network methods (to_*, read_*), code-evaluating ones (eval, query, pipe, format), inplace and the walrus operator, and evaluates with empty builtins on a deep copy. The number guard exists because the 4B model got the right number from pandas but wrote it wrong, for example “thirteen hundred and forty-four” for 314. A failed check gets one correction round; then the app prints the exact figures itself. Tool rounds use thinking mode, which picked much better queries at 2 to 7 seconds per answer.

Titanic · Tech talk10
Claude Code built the project end to end from a written brief, showing a plan before touching files. The debugging that mattered most came from running things for real: live Ollama questions exposed the number problem; browser screenshots exposed a CSS bug where a tilted main element trapped the fixed-position flood overlay. The dataviz skill guided the chart palette, validated for colour-blind separation. Humans set the vision, approved the plan, and made the format calls.

Titanic · Tech talk11
The biggest gap is measurement for the chatbot: today we have eight hand-checked questions, not a benchmark. An evaluation set with expected pandas results would let us compare models and prompts. Streaming would hide the 2 to 7 second wait. CI and a Docker image make it shareable; self-hosting fonts and Plotly makes it work fully offline.
